Routes only main human limb body parts into limb structural complication checks.
Very small independent chances of deeper damage beneath a minor blunt wound.
Massive blunt trauma can independently damage muscle, joint-support structures, nerves, bone, and the tissue compartment.
Bone injury already exists; only surrounding soft-tissue complications are rolled.
A devastating ballistic wound can produce several independent structural injuries at once.
Electrical injuries damage nerves without using anatomical nerve severance as an outcome.
Only runs once a bite-specific wound has been created by bite routing.
Torso structural rolls are separate from limb rolls and may independently produce chest-wall, internal, and hemorrhagic injuries.
Extreme torso blunt trauma may produce chest-wall trauma, internal organ trauma, and internal hemorrhage independently.
No instant-death roll: devastating penetration produces severe persistent complications instead.
Devastating torso ballistics can create multiple severe but non-instantly-fatal long-term complications.
Public structural-complication entry point. The wound bridge should call this with the body part and newly created wound id.
